text:
Maria Gomez: heads up — our payments service started throwing AccessDenied on KMS decrypt after we switched to using an assumed role for cross-account access. console/developer users can decrypt fine. anyone seen something like this with grant tokens or session policies?

Tyler Chen: do we have an error snippet from CloudTrail or the service logs? that narrows it.

Maria Gomez: CloudTrail shows KMS AccessDenied for Decrypt. message: "User: arn:aws:sts::111222333:assumed-role/payments-app/ci-runner is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:444555666:key/abcd-ef01"

Aj Patel: is the call using a grant token? sometimes when grants are issued, Decrypt requires passing grant token if the grant hasn't fully propagated or if key policy expects it.

Maria Gomez: the app does not send any grant token. the key was rotated & we issued a new grant for the cross-account role last week. i tried aws kms decrypt locally with the assumed role credentials and get the same AccessDenied.

Olivia Ramos: can you paste the key policy and the role trust/policy? obv redact ARNs if you want.

Maria Gomez: here's the minimal key policy and role policy (redacted ids):

```json
KeyPolicy:
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowUseByPaymentsRole",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::444555666:role/payments-cross-account"},
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:Encrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}

RolePolicy (attached to payments-cross-account):
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["kms:Decrypt","kms:Encrypt"],"Resource":"arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:444555666:key/abcd-ef01"}
  ]
}
```

Aj Patel: that looks fine at first glance. two things to check: 1) does the role session have a session policy or session tags that might restrict kms actions? 2) were any grants created with constraints (e.g., encryptionContext) that require a grant token?

Maria Gomez: good call — we use STS assume-role with a session policy embedded by the token vending service. session policy denies kms:Decrypt except when executed by the "payments-service" principal. maybe the session principal string is different once assumed?

Tyler Chen: show the assume-role command you use in CI and the resulting caller identity.

Maria Gomez: we do: 
```bash
aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::444555666:role/payments-cross-account --role-session-name ci-123 --duration-seconds 3600 --serial-number arn:aws:iam::111222333:mfa/user --token-code 123456
```
and caller identity returns: 
```json
{"Arn":"arn:aws:sts::111222333:assumed-role/payments-cross-account/ci-123","Account":"111222333","UserId":"AROAI...:ci-123"}
```

Olivia Ramos: the key policy principal was the role ARN in account 444555666. but the assumed role ARN above shows account 111222333. cross-account access requires the key policy to permit the *principal* that will be calling, which for cross-account is the account/principal in the caller account or the IAM role in the key account depending on trust. hmm.

Aj Patel: another angle: are there active grants on that key? run `aws kms list-grants --key-id <key-id>` with creds from the key account. if a grant exists that targets the principal and requires passing a grant token, it might cause Decrypt to fail unless the token is provided.

Maria Gomez: ran list-grants from the key owner account — there is a grant for the role, created by our infra runbook:
```json
{
  "GranteePrincipal": "arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/payments-cross-account",
  "GrantId": "g-0123456789abcdef",
  "Operations": ["Decrypt","Encrypt"]
}
```

Maria Gomez: but when I call decrypt as the assumed-role principal (from account 111...), kms returns AccessDenied.

Tyler Chen: two likely causes: 1) the key policy's Principal might not match the exact principal string used in the call (assumed-role vs role ARN differences), or 2) the session policy attached to the STS call is explicitly denying Decrypt. check CloudTrail to see if the event includes a `DeniedBy` field or `sessionPolicy` failure reason.

sec-bot: Audit note: 2026-03-19T14:07:12Z - KMS Decrypt API call denied for arn:aws:sts::111222333:assumed-role/payments-cross-account/ci-123. KeyId: abcd-ef01. Refer to KMS KeyPolicy and IAM session policies.

Aj Patel: can you try decrypt while passing the grant token (just to test) — use `--grant-tokens g-0123456789abcdef` with the assumed creds. if decrypt succeeds, that indicates grant propagation/token requirement.

Maria Gomez: tried that and got the same AccessDenied.

Olivia Ramos: then not a grant-token propagation issue. What's the key's key-state? Was it reimported or re-enabled after rotation? if the key is pending deletion or disabled, KMS can deny.

Maria Gomez: Key state: Enabled. Rotation timeline: we rotated the CMK last week and added a new grant. The role policy references the key ARN.

Tyler Chen: one subtlety: if the key policy explicitly lists the principal as the role ARN in the key account (arn:aws:iam::444555666:role/payments-cross-account) but the caller is an assumed role from a different account (arn:aws:sts::111222333:assumed-role/payments-cross-account/ci-123), the Principal in key policy must reference the calling principal (the role in the caller account) or be a wildcard for the account. For cross-account, it's common to allow the entire account: "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111222333:root" or the role ARN in the caller account.

Aj Patel: yep — key policy principal must match the caller identity. update the key policy to include the 111222333 role ARN or the account principal. Also ensure there's no explicit Deny in the session policy.

Maria Gomez: that explains it — when we created the key policy we accidentally used the role ARN from the key account (444...) instead of allowing the external caller account/role. fixing now to add `arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/payments-cross-account` into the key policy principal.

Olivia Ramos: after change, test with `aws kms decrypt` using the assumed creds. also check CloudTrail to confirm allow.

Maria Gomez: update applied, rerunning tests...

sec-bot: Audit note: 2026-03-19T14:17:58Z - KeyPolicy updated by Maria Gomez (console).

Maria Gomez: decrypt now succeeds from CI assumed role. thanks all. leaving a note in infra runbook to use account-level principals for cross-account keys to avoid this confusion. :white_check_mark:

Tyler Chen: nice catch. add that to security playbook and maybe a quick linter for key policies.

Aj Patel: gap closed.
